correctness.rationale: The uniform Dirichlet cardinal identity solves for the deleted sample with positive coefficient D_m(delta h)/N. Substitution gives the unique weights on the distinct grid. The sine quotient has alternating sign and, at any odd fixed j>=3, the circular distance to delta is strictly greater than delta; even j have positive weights above 1/N. Only j=1 reaches zero at half a mesh. The norm is the absolute weight sum, attained by choosing the data signs to match the weights. In the row Gram matrix the unchanged rows give an identity block; the new unit row has projection of squared length 1-c_N^2 onto their span, so the nontrivial block has the stated eigenvalues, with all eigenvalues one at delta=0. At fixed t with delta_N=1-t/N, the sine ratio divided by N tends to 1/t and Nc_N tends to t, giving both limits. Independent direct moment solves and SVD corroborate the finite diagnostic at small and moderate grids. The frozen limitation incorrectly suggested mere nonuniqueness at delta=1: every sample of D_m then vanishes while its integral is one. The complete corrected files state nonexistence at the excluded endpoint, clarify the norm-attaining data and distinguish the mesh gap t/N from the angular gap 2*pi*t/N^2. The theorem on its original domain is unchanged.
residual_risks: The exact signs apply to a single moved node on the odd grid and to precisely the specified trigonometric space; neither arbitrary jitter nor the singular endpoint is covered. The numerical checks are supplementary, not a uniform proof.

value.rationale: For exactly band-limited samples, the positivity radius and sharp data-noise norm provide an exact diagnostic that broad conditioning bounds cannot give. One can have bounded sample-to-integral amplification at a gap of order N^(-2) in angle while full coefficient recovery has linearly growing condition number. The distinction between these two tasks and the absence of any exact rule at the collision are mathematically meaningful boundaries, not simply a condition-number calculation.
residual_risks: The diagnostic is for the specified one-node path; it does not imply noise stability on general nonuniform grids or at the singular endpoint.
